question: Which wastewater plants should Horton call first?
html:
Horton should call New Haven East Shore, Hartford and Norwalk first. All three are Connecticut plants with work already on the state's fundable list, in Horton's home market (CET wastewater-plant targets). MWRA Deer Island and Bridgeport Westside come next.

First-call list

RankPlantFitFundable workRequested work
1New Haven East Shore (40 MGD)98$82M wet-weather/odor control, FY27$19.2M process-air compressors
2Hartford WPCF (60 MGD)96$24.3M sludge screening/equalization, FY26-27$31.6M Island Road, Hog Brook pump stations
3Norwalk WPCF (18 MGD)95$26M final settling tanks, FY27$48M green aeration
4MWRA Deer Island94$289M Clarifier #2 in the 2026 IUP—
5Bridgeport Westside (30 MGD)93Not shown in the excerptNot shown

(CET wastewater-plant targets)

Why these three lead

  • Funding is real. CT dollars split into two groups. Table 2 / Category I items are on the fundable list. Table 3 items are only requests eligible for first-come reserves. Each top-three plant has fundable work plus a larger request behind it (CET wastewater-plant targets).
  • Norwalk fits the cross-sell. Aeration is the plant's biggest energy load, so the $48M request pairs Horton electrical with NuWave efficiency.
  • Phase 1 of the growth plan names these plants. It points Horton at 62 funded or requested projects and leads with New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk (CET growth plan).

Signals on the next tier

  • Deer Island: the plant already self-generates 26% of its electricity. The angle is electrical subcontracting plus storage and efficiency, not solar.
  • Bridgeport Westside: EPA shows 12 quarters with noncompliance and 1 with significant noncompliance. Its permit is administratively continued past June 30, 2024, and the last inspection was 683 days ago (EPA wastewater-plant compliance). Read this as a possible sign of capital need (est.), not a confirmed project.
  • Permit timing: Norwalk's permit expired March 31, 2026. New Haven and Hartford permits are administratively continued (EPA wastewater-plant compliance). Renewals can bring scope changes (est.), but the data do not tie any project to them.

Gaps to close

  • Pipeline totals by plant. Only Hartford ($105.7M) and Norwalk ($76.5M) are fully visible.
  • Bridgeport Westside's project detail, which is cut off in the excerpt.
  • Bid and procurement dates for each fundable item. These set the actual call order.
  • Any existing Horton relationships with GNHWPCA and MDC.

Next actions

  1. Confirm the procurement stage and engineer of record for New Haven's $82M, Hartford's $24.3M and Norwalk's $26M projects.
  2. Pair Horton and NuWave on one Norwalk aeration pitch, with a joint electrical and efficiency scope.
  3. Pull Bridgeport Westside's full project record and Deer Island's Clarifier #2 subcontracting plan before outreach.
  4. Map Horton's existing contacts at the top five operators and assign an owner for each call.
